description: Remote transit. Reader half of 08-transit-local, to run on the far host against the domain the RDMA transfer lands in. Same flow id, same two reader lanes, no writer. stamp.transit_ms now spans two machines, so it is only meaningful if both clocks are disciplined to the same PTP/TAI source -- an unsynchronised pair reports the clock offset, not the transport. Start it once the flow is visible in the local domain (mxl-info -d); the writer runs 20 min, so there is time to bring RDMA up first.

B.note: diagnostic only; the lane does not branch on it. is_active:false here means the flow has no writer in THIS domain yet
the first grain not yet written; every read after this blocks on the writer instead of racing it
blocking, so the loop is paced by the writer itself -- no delay_before_ms

C.note: always jumps to the newest committed grain, so this lane can never desync; its transit carries up to one commit interval of extra age

name: 09-transit-remote-reader
